query:

Use this retrieval strategy, and follow it rather than opening listings in the order they appear.
1. Read the advertised price of every listing above first. That price is the cheapest option that listing can sell, so nothing it can sell costs less.
2. Open listings in ascending order of advertised price. For each one, choose size M, then look at the page again and read the price it now shows. The price a listing shows before you choose is its cheapest option that can be bought, not necessarily the one asked about, and the reply to choosing an option does not show the new price. Then check whether that option can actually be bought. An option can be listed and still be unavailable, in which case it is shown as disabled or greyed out and cannot be chosen from the menu, so it has no price you can use.
3. Keep the 3 cheapest available totals you have found so far, each with its seller. A cheaper unavailable one changes nothing.
4. Once you hold 3, skip every unopened listing whose advertised price is at or above the dearest of those 3 totals. Such a listing cannot enter the 3 whatever its stock.
5. Stop when you hold 3 and no unopened listing has an advertised price below the dearest of them. If fewer than 3 listings have the option available, you must open every listing, and then say so and name those that do.
In your answer, list the 3 sellers in order with the price of each, say explicitly that you checked each option was available rather than only listed, and say how many listings you opened, how many you skipped, and why skipping them was safe.
Important: the figure this bound produces is a limit used only to decide what to skip. It is not a price read for the option asked about, and must never appear in your answer as one. Only report a price you read from a listing you opened, for the exact option asked about, read after that option was chosen. Never pair an advertised price with an option unless you saw that price shown while that option was chosen.

result.final:
The 3 cheapest sellers of the Larchmere Heavyweight Cotton Tee in size M that can actually ship it, in order:

1. Elmsworth Apparel — $19.17
2. Everleigh Threads — $21.54
3. Bexhill Textiles Official Store — $21.71

I verified each option was available, not merely listed: on every listing I opened the size menu, and only counted sellers where the M option was present and enabled (not disabled/greyed out), could be selected, the page then showed a concrete price for size M after selection, and Add to Cart remained active.

I opened 8 of the 21 tee listings, in ascending order of advertised price: Brindle Clothing Co ($14.18, no M option), Lymington Uniform Supply ($15.18, M disabled), Dunmore Garments ($16.45, no M option), Bexhill Textiles Official Store ($16.75, M available at $21.71), Elmsworth Apparel ($17.83, M available at $19.17), Haldane Garment Works ($17.97, M disabled), Northwick Clothing Co ($18.16, M disabled), and Everleigh Threads ($19.05, M available at $21.54). Once I held 3 available totals (dearest = $21.71), I skipped the remaining 13 unopened listings — Pentland Apparel Official Store ($23.78) through Dovercourt Threads ($41.55) — because every one of them has an advertised price at or above $21.71. That skip was safe because the advertised price is the cheapest price that listing sells at; the size-M price can never be below it, so none of those listings could enter the top 3 regardless of its stock. Stopping was also safe: no unopened listing had an advertised price below the dearest of my 3 held totals.
